title: invocation-safety-net: canary guardrails for structured-output and function-invocation compatibility
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement an "invocation safety net" that prevents incompatible structured-output or function-invocation changes from reaching production during canary/A-B/shadow rollouts. The feature will run automated compatibility checks (schema validation, function-signature diffs, required-argument checks, and example-driven contract tests) in the runtime and console so rollouts can auto-fail and rollback when compatibility regressions are detected.
goals: Detect incompatible changes to function-call signatures and structured output contracts before full rollout
Fail fast and auto-rollback canaries that show >X% contract violations
Provide clear developer-visible diffs and suggested mitigations in the Console and rollout logs
Integrate with existing shadow traffic harness and A/B experiment framework
non_goals: Full static type inference or deep semantic validation of arbitrary JSON payloads
technical_approach: At serving time, augment request/response pipeline with a contract-checker plugin that extracts declared function schemas and structured-output contracts from the model manifest
Run lightweight validation: required fields, field type families (string/number/object/array), enum presence, and presence/absence of function_name/arguments when function-calling is used
Compute a compact function-signature fingerprint per model version and store historical fingerprints in the rollout metadata index
During canary/shadow traffic, compute signature diffs between baseline and candidate; surface diff counts and examples to Console
If contract-violation rate exceeds configurable threshold (default 0.5%), mark canary as failing and trigger auto-rollback and alerting
acceptance_criteria: Contract-checker runs in the request path for canary traffic with <1ms median overhead on p95-serving latency for short responses
Console shows a per-canary compatibility dashboard with diff histogram, failing examples, and suggested fallback policy
Auto-rollback triggers when violations > threshold and rollback completes within configured timeout
A/B experiment reports include contract-violation lift relative to baseline
End-to-end tests cover schema detection for at least 6 common patterns (optional fields, renamed keys, nested arrays, enum changes, missing function args, extra args)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local runner integration (owner: ENG-Backend)
Phase 1 (internal): enable on internal canaries only, collect metrics for 72h, no auto-rollback (owner: ENG-Backend)
Phase 2 (staged): enable auto-rollback for internal and low-traffic external canaries (1% traffic), run for 1 week
Phase 3 (gradual): raise to 10% canary coverage with alerts to oncall, require security review for customers requesting opt-in
Phase 4 (ga): default enablement for new model rollouts with per-project opt-out
telemetry_and_alerting: Metric: contract_violations_per_1000_calls (tagged by model, version, canary_id)
Alert: contract_violation_rate > threshold for 5m => PagerDuty to SRE + product oncall
Dashboard: per-route heatmap with failing-example sampler and top-5 changed fields
failure_modes_and_mitigation: False positives due to fuzzy type checks => mitigation: add example-driven heuristics and allowlist stable fields
Performance regressions when response size is large => mitigation: sample responses and run full validation asynchronously with a best-effort estimator in-path
Schema changes that are intended (backwards-compatible additions) erroneously cause rollback => mitigation: allow configurable compat rules (additive-only, tolerant enums) per project
Missing manifests causing checker to skip => mitigation: fail-canary-if-manifest-missing option

Run shadow traffic harness and verify violations are logged and sampled examples are attached

notes: Prefer sampling for large responses to avoid p95 overhead spikes
